verdicts.summary: The combined rev-parse only trusts its output when the exit code is 0 or 1 and the line count matches. Every other case goes back to the old separate commands.
verdicts.scenario: I tried five cases. (1) Git older than 2.31 echoes `--path-format=absolute`. Output is 5 lines with HEAD or 4 without, against an expected 4 or 3, so it falls back. (2) A path containing a newline adds one line, and exit 0 versus 1 fixes the expected count, so the counts cannot coincide and it falls back. (3) Exit 128 outside a repo, or a transient failure: `headChecked` is false, so `resolveGitCommonDir` runs and throws the same error as before, and `hasHeadCommit` supplies `headExists`. (4) The capture retry and the darwin fsync retry. Neither fires on the new call, because it uses `allowNonZeroExit` and the retry guard at VcsProcess.ts:282 requires `!allowNonZeroExit`. The old `resolveGitCommonDir` and `hasHeadCommit` calls ran under other operation labels, so they were not retried either. (5) Metrics and output size. Exit 1 on an unborn HEAD is not counted as a failure, because `failedExit` needs `!allowNonZeroExit`. The 1,000,000-byte default output cap cannot truncate a few path lines.
